title: Editor: Dock resize handles freeze when moved rapidly while 3D Viewport is active
body:
### Tested versions

I only tested this in Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045), I had no issue with this on 4.5 or 4.5.1.

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4790K CPU @ 4.00GHz (8 threads) - 31.93 GiB memory

### Issue description

When the 3D Viewport is active, when attempting to resize the Editor Docks (such as the Inspector or Scene Tree or Bottom Dock Tray) by dragging the splitter bar, it "locks up" if the mouse is moved quickly.

If the mouse moves at a high velocity, the handle stops following the cursor, and the dock remains stuck in its current position. Resizing works as expected only when moving the mouse slowly. This suggests the mouse cursor is escaping the splitter bar's grabber area before the engine can update the panel width.

This issue does not occur when using the 2D, Script, or Asset Library tabs. It appears to be exclusive to the 3D editor mode.

### Steps to reproduce

Open any Godot project.
Go in the 3D Tab.
Click and hold the splitter bar between the Inspector and the 3D Viewport.
Move the mouse horizontally very quickly. Observe that the handle "freezes" and stops following the cursor.
Switch to the 2D Tab or Script Tab.
Repeat the same rapid movement. Observe that the resizing works perfectly without freezing.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

"N/A - This is an Editor UI issue specifically tied to the 3D Viewport's active state. It occurs in any project, including a fresh empty project, as long as the 3D tab is selected."
